formulas.name: Single-Point Fault Metric (SPFM)
formulas.expression: SPFM = 1 - (Σ λ_SPF + Σ λ_RF) / (Σ λ_SPF + Σ λ_RF + Σ λ_MPF,D + Σ λ_MPF,L + Σ λ_S)

variables.meaning: failure rate of single-point faults
failure rate of residual faults
failure rate of detected multiple-point faults
failure rate of latent multiple-point faults
failure rate of safe faults

formulas.worked_example: Element 1: λ_SPF=5, λ_RF=3, λ_MPF,D=10, λ_MPF,L=2, λ_S=80 FIT. Element 2: λ_SPF=2, λ_RF=1, λ_MPF,D=5, λ_MPF,L=1, λ_S=41 FIT. Numerator: Σ(λ_SPF+λ_RF)=7+4=11 FIT. Denominator: 7+4+15+3+121=150 FIT. SPFM = 1 - 11/150 = 1 - 0.073333 = 0.926667 = 92.67%. ASIL B target (≥90%) is met; ASIL C target (≥97%) is not met.
formulas.clause_locator: Annex C (normative), Clause 8 Table 4 for targets
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact table number for target values in Clause 8 is inferred from standard structure but not directly verified; the formula expression is the normative Annex C version.

formulas.name: Latent-Fault Metric (LFM)
formulas.expression: LFM = 1 - Σ λ_MPF,L / (Σ λ_MPF,L + Σ λ_MPF,D + Σ λ_S)

variables.meaning: failure rate of latent multiple-point faults
failure rate of detected multiple-point faults
failure rate of safe faults

formulas.worked_example: Same elements as SPFM example: Σ λ_MPF,L=3 FIT, Σ λ_MPF,D=15 FIT, Σ λ_S=121 FIT. Denominator: 3+15+121=139 FIT. LFM = 1 - 3/139 = 1 - 0.021583 = 0.978417 = 97.84%. ASIL C target (≥80%) and ASIL D target (≥90%) are both met.
formulas.clause_locator: Annex C (normative), Clause 8 Table 5 for targets
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact table number for target values in Clause 8 is inferred; the denominator expression is equivalent to (Σ λ_total - Σ λ_SPF - Σ λ_RF).

formulas.name: Probabilistic Metric for Hardware Failure (PMHF)
formulas.expression: PMHF = Σ λ_SPF + Σ λ_RF + (Σ λ_DPF,latent × Σ λ_DPF,det × T_lifetime) / 10^9, with all λ in FIT and T_lifetime in hours

variables.meaning: failure rate of single-point faults
failure rate of residual faults
failure rate of latent dual-point faults
failure rate of detected dual-point faults
operational lifetime of the item

formulas.worked_example: Σ λ_SPF=7 FIT, Σ λ_RF=4 FIT, Σ λ_DPF,latent=3 FIT, Σ λ_DPF,det=15 FIT, T_lifetime=100000 h. First two terms: 7+4=11 FIT. Dual-point term: (3×15×100000)/10^9 = 4,500,000/10^9 = 0.0045 FIT. PMHF = 11 + 0.0045 = 11.0045 FIT. This meets ASIL B and C targets (≤100 FIT) but not ASIL D (≤10 FIT).
formulas.clause_locator: Clause 9 / Annex F.2 (simplified), Clause 8 Table 6 for targets
formulas.known_uncertainty: This is the simplified Annex F.2 formula; the full normative PMHF calculation in Clause 9 involves probabilistic integration over the operational lifetime and diagnostic test intervals, which is more complex than this algebraic approximation.

edge_cases: Σ λ_total = 0 (no safety-related hardware elements): SPFM and LFM denominators become zero; calculator must abort and report undefined.
T_lifetime = 0: PMHF dual-point term collapses to zero, leaving only SPF+RF contributions; calculator should warn that lifetime must be positive.
SPFM exactly at threshold boundary (e.g., 90.000% for ASIL B): standard uses ≥, so equality passes; PMHF uses <, so equality at exactly 10 FIT for ASIL D fails.

formulas.name: Chi-squared upper-confidence-bound FIT rate

variables.meaning: chi-squared statistic at confidence level %CL with (2f+2) degrees of freedom
number of observed failures during test
test duration per device
sample size (number of devices tested)
acceleration factor from stress to use conditions

formulas.worked_example: ss=231, t=1000 h, f=0, 60% confidence level. Degrees of freedom: 2×0+2=2. χ²_0.60,2 = 1.8326. AF=77.6 (from Arrhenius example). Denominator: 2×1000×231×77.6 = 35,851,200. λ_CL = (1.8326×10^9) / 35,851,200 = 51.1 FIT.
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact JESD85 section number is not verified; the χ² value depends on the statistical table or function implementation used.

formulas.name: Arrhenius acceleration factor

variables.meaning: apparent activation energy of the failure mechanism
Boltzmann constant
absolute use temperature
absolute stress test temperature

formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact JESD85 section number is not verified; typical E_a=0.7 eV is a broad industry default but actual values range from ~0.3 eV (electromigration) to ~1.0 eV (oxide breakdown), and using the wrong E_a can over- or under-accelerate by orders of magnitude.

edge_cases: ss=0 or t=0 or AF=0: denominator becomes zero; calculator must reject input.
T_stress ≤ T_use: AF ≤ 1, which is physically valid only if the stress temperature does not accelerate the mechanism; calculator should warn that AF < 1 implies no acceleration or invalid input.
f=0 with 0% confidence level: χ²_0,2 = 0, yielding λ_CL = 0, which is an uninformative lower bound; calculator should require a positive confidence level.

formulas.name: Total Processing Performance (TPP)

variables.meaning: theoretical peak Tera operations per second for multiply-accumulate computation (D=A×B+C) of processing unit i
largest bit-length of the inputs to the multiply operation for processing unit i
number of digital processing units on the integrated circuit

formulas.worked_example: Processing unit 1: MacTOPS=50, bit_length=16 → TPP1=2×50×16=1600. Processing unit 2: MacTOPS=25, bit_length=8 → TPP2=2×25×8=400. Total TPP = 1600+400 = 2000.
formulas.authority: EAR Supplement No. 4 to Part 774, Technical Note 1 to ECCN 3A090
formulas.clause_locator: 15 CFR Part 774 Supplement No. 4, Technical Note 1
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact CFR citation for the Technical Note is inferred from EAR structure; the formula wording is verbatim from BIS guidance but the formal Federal Register citation may differ.

formulas.name: Performance Density (PD)

variables.meaning: total processing performance of the integrated circuit
area in mm² of all logic dies manufactured with a non-planar transistor architecture on the integrated circuit

formulas.authority: EAR Supplement No. 4 to Part 774, Technical Note 4 to ECCN 3A090
formulas.clause_locator: 15 CFR Part 774 Supplement No. 4, Technical Note 4
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact CFR citation for the Technical Note is inferred; the definition of applicable_die_area excludes separate memory stacks (e.g., HBM) per BIS guidance.

formulas.name: ECCN 3A090 classification thresholds
formulas.expression: 3A090.a if TPP ≥ 4800 OR (TPP ≥ 1600 AND PD ≥ 5.92); 3A090.b if (TPP ≥ 2400 AND TPP < 4800 AND PD ≥ 1.6 AND PD < 5.92) OR (TPP ≥ 1600 AND PD ≥ 3.2 AND PD < 5.92)

variables.meaning: total processing performance
performance density

formulas.worked_example: TPP=2000, PD=5.0. 3A090.a: 2000<4800 and 5.0<5.92 → false. 3A090.b: first branch 2000<2400 → false; second branch 2000≥1600 AND 5.0≥3.2 AND 5.0<5.92 → true. Result: ECCN 3A090.b.
formulas.authority: BIS Interim Final Rule (AI Diffusion IFR, January 2025) and subsequent amendments
formulas.known_uncertainty: Threshold values are current as of April 2025 BIS guidance; an interim final rule was pending finalization and thresholds may have been revised between April 2025 and August 2026.

edge_cases: applicable_die_area = 0: division by zero; calculator must reject because die area must be positive.
MacTOPS = 0 or bit_length = 0 for all units: TPP = 0, which is below all thresholds; calculator should return uncontrolled.
TPP or PD exactly at threshold boundary: regulation uses ≥ and < with exact numeric boundaries; equality on a lower bound pushes into the higher control tier.

formulas.name: Advanced manufacturing investment credit (48D)

variables.meaning: basis of qualified property placed in service by the taxpayer that is part of an advanced manufacturing facility

formulas.known_uncertainty: Statute was amended by Pub. L. 119-21 in 2025 to substitute 35% for 25%; no further amendments are verified as of August 2026, but tax legislation is subject to frequent change.

edge_cases: qualified_investment = 0: credit = 0; this is valid but the calculator should flag that no credit is generated.

No pure-calculation statutory threshold exists for the primary-purpose test in § 48D(b)(3); the 75% illustrative threshold appears only in proposed regulations, not the statute, so a calculator cannot apply a hard numeric cutoff without regulatory guidance.
Negative qualified investment: not physically meaningful for basis; calculator must reject negative input.
